meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: federal common-law statutory framework under the Canada Business Corporations Act, combined with Quebec's civil-law tradition applicable to private law; Quebec provincial incorporations are governed by the Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1.

Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement between Canada and the European Union (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal AML/CFT: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, and its regulations, including the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 152.1 et seq. (register of individuals with significant control for federal corporations). Quebec: Act respecting the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, CQLR c L-25.1, and its regulation; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1 (register of natural persons having significant control and related corporate records).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable for foreign documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the Canadian Criminal Code terrorist entity list, sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, and the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, and applicable EU/UK lists where there is a foreign nexus. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person (PEP), domestic PEP under FINTRAC guidelines, sanctions hit, adverse media, or anomalous source-of-funds explanation. Results must be documented in the AML/CFT pre-incorporation file and retained according to the PCMLTFA record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Federal: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre, including the NUANS name search and name reservation service; Quebec: Registraire des entreprises - Registre des entreprises du Quebec (https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, a Quebec provincial corporate name must be in French; non-French names or bilingual names require a French version and must comply with the standards of the Office quebecois de la langue francaise. A federal CBCA name may be in English, French, or bilingual, but before extraprovincial registration or carrying on business in Quebec, the name must be registered with the Registraire des entreprises and comply with Quebec language law. All names must use Latin characters, may include digits and recognized French accents, and must include an appropriate legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltee', 'Limitée', or equivalent, depending on the governing statute.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporations (federal) or the Registraire des entreprises (Quebec) rejects the proposed name, the applicant may make written submissions in support of reconsideration within 15 days of the notice of refusal. If the initial refusal is maintained, the applicant may file an administrative review request; thereafter, a judicial review application may be made to the Federal Court of Canada (for CBCA names) or the Superior Court of Quebec (for Quebec corporate names) within 30 days of the final administrative decision. In all cases, before restarting the name clearance process, a fresh NUANS report should be ordered because previously searched names may have been taken during the appeal period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this non-regulated trading-card publishing activity only if the registered office is a real physical address in Canada or Quebec, as applicable, and is not a post-office box; a virtual office or registered-agent service may accept service of process and maintain corporate records, but substance and books-and-records obligations must be satisfied at that physical location. CRA and the Registraire des entreprises may reject a mere mail-forwarding address or a virtual office with no responsible person physically available.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: for a non-regulated, non-financial business corporation in the collectible trading-card sector, the likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registraire des entreprises or CRA is estimated at less than 5% in the first year. If a virtual office or shared-office address is declared, the probability of an address-verification contact or unannounced compliance visit increases to approximately 10-15%. Regulatory inspection risk rises immediately if the company conducts cash-heavy transactions, invites public foot traffic, or adopts a name implying financial services.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, as amended, principally ss. 5, 8-9, 31, 92 and 312; alternative federal incorporation available under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c. C-44, ss. 6-17.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Enterprises), Government of Québec
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed electronically with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, together with the enterprise registration declaration (déclaration d'immatriculation) and issuance of the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; shares may be issued for nominal consideration in cash, property or services; no escrow account is required; the stated paid-up capital must be fully paid before share issuance and evidenced by share subscription records.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the share subscription presented to the Board is APPROVED and the Secretary is directed to issue the subscribed shares to the subscribers upon payment of full consideration; (2) That the registered office of the Corporation is established at [address], Province of Quebec, and the Registrar of Enterprises is directed to record such address; (3) That the following persons are APPOINTED to the offices set opposite their names: President, Secretary, and Treasurer; and each officer is vested with authority to execute all documents required to conduct the Corporation's business; and (4) That the directors approve the by-laws and authorize the officers to open banking accounts and make all necessary filings required by law. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online Name Research and Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search through the REQ portal to confirm that the proposed corporate name is distinctive, not confusingly similar to any existing name, and not prohibited under the QBCA. File the name reservation request, pay the statutory reservation fee, and obtain the name reservation report, which is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Name research request formulated on the REQ online form
Signed declaration of the applicant confirming that the proposed name is not prohibited
Payment of the statutory name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a refusal, review the stated grounds, submit an amended name research with new distinctive elements within the prescribed response period, or file a written request for reconsideration with REQ detailing why the name should be accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel; REQ as the receiving registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statutory Articles of Incorporation in the form prescribed under the QBCA, including the corporate name, registered office address, authorized share structure, classes and rights of shares, permitted restrictions (if any), and the particulars of the founding directors. Have the incorporator sign the articles before a witness and obtain signed written consents from all founding directors.
required_dossiers: Duly executed Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs)
Written Consent to Act as Director executed by each founding director
Notice of the corporate head office (siège social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ queries the submission for incomplete data or missing consents, file the corrective documents through the same electronic channel within the prescribed period; if the articles are rejected for defective witnessing, re-execute the articles before a competent witness or a notary and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Electronic Filing Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the signed PDF of the Articles of Incorporation to the REQ online filing service, complete the enterprise registration declaration with the head office address and director/officer information, and pay the statutory filing fees online. Upon processing, REQ will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and assign the nine-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: PDF of the signed Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ sends an information request (demande de renseignements), respond in writing through the portal within the stated period and supply the requested verification; if the name reservation has expired due to processing delay, request a waiver or obtain a new reservation before filing is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Post-Incorporation Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation (directors and officers), Revenu Québec, CNESST, and the local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors to adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution, fix the registered office address, approve the issuance of subscribed shares, appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer, adopt the model by-laws, and authorize officers to open bank accounts. Afterward, register with Revenu Québec for GST/QST and source deductions, register with CNESST if employing workers, and apply for the municipal business licence for the printing and production premises.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first meeting of directors
Register of directors and officers, including signed consents
Certificate of Incorporation and confirmation of NEQ
Tenant lease or landlord occupancy consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a post-incorporation registration is rejected because of missing supporting documents, cure the deficiency on the relevant online portal or in person and resubmit; for municipal licensing delays linked to zoning or occupancy, request an interim permit once the fire safety inspection and structural occupancy review are completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable at the provincial level for trading-card cold-foil printing; local municipal permit office exercises business licensing authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal business licence (permis d'entreprise) issued under the Cities and Towns Act, CQLR c. C-19, together with any required occupancy certificate (certificat d'occupation)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Government of Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for small-scale printing and packaging operations; subject to registration and declaration obligations under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2) only where solvent or VOC usage exceeds the de minimis regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: comply with municipal sewer by-laws, typically pH 6.5-9.5, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 50 mg/L; Air: maintain volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions below 1 metric tonne per year to remain outside the Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1) permit tiers; Waste: store and dispose of inks, solvents and empty drums as hazardous residual materials under the Hazardous Materials Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 32), with manifest records for any off-site transport.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire safety service verifying compliance with the Quebec Fire Safety Code; structural load and occupancy inspection clearance for press and foil equipment; workplace health and safety registration and clearance from the CNESST under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (CQLR c. S-2.1), including machine guarding, chemical safety data sheets, and personal protective equipment programs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for GST/HST and federal corporate income tax; Revenu Québec for QST (Quebec Sales Tax), Quebec corporate income tax, and business registration; Portals: CRA My Business Account (canada.ca) and Revenu Québec CléInfo Business Portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a business corporation federally (Corporations Canada) or in Quebec (Registraire des entreprises), or register the foreign entity as an extra-provincial branch. Step 2: Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and open a GST/HST account through CRA Form RC1 or the online Non-Resident GST/HST Registration application. Step 3: Register for QST with Revenu Québec via CléInfo using Form LM-3 or the online business registration service where the corporation carries on taxable commercial activity in Quebec. Step 4: Open federal and Quebec corporate income tax accounts (CRA RT account and Revenu Québec RP account). Issuance time is typically 15 to 20 business days. Non-resident suppliers of cross-border supplies may use the simplified CRA e-commerce GST/HST registration framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election. Relevant statutory elections include: GST/HST closely related persons election under Excise Tax Act s.156, GST/HST and QST joint venture elections (ETA s.273; QSTA s.439.9), corporate amalgamation and winding-up rollover elections (ITA s.87 and s.88), non-resident deemed-disposition elections, and hybrid-mismatch compliance provisions under ITA ss.94.5 to 94.8. Foreign entity classification follows Canadian domestic character rules (e.g., a foreign LLC is generally treated as a corporation unless a clear flow-through character is established under its home jurisdiction law).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and QST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax plus Quebec Sales Tax) - VAT-model consumption taxes
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - small-supplier threshold under GST/HST (ETA s.148) and QST (QSTA s.29.2); a registrant is required once taxable worldwide revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters; non-resident suppliers selling to Canadian consumers apply the same CAD 30,000 threshold under the 2021 e-commerce alignment rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal or Quebec real-time e-invoicing, API fiscal clearance, or digital stamping mandate applies to the manufacture, printing, or publishing of collectible trading cards. Electronic invoices are legally recognized under the Quebec Act respecting the legal framework of information technology (RLRQ c. C-1.1) with the recipient's consent. CRA and Revenu Québec require six years of books and records retention. Sector-specific certified sales-recording software requirements in Quebec apply only to designated service businesses (e.g., meal services), not to exporting card manufacturers or publishers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Collectible trading cards, being tangible personal property, are zero-rated under s.22 of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act, and correspondingly exempt under s.106 of the QSTA, where the supplier physically exports the goods or delivers them to a common carrier for export from Canada. Holographic cold-foil printing and publishing services supplied to a non-resident recipient are zero-rated under Part V, s.9 of Schedule VI to the ETA if the benefit of the service is consumed outside Canada. Full input tax credits (ITCs) and QST refunds are available to the manufacturer/publisher on inputs used in zero-rated export supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / CBSA Export Report (G13 CAED, ACI eManifest, or approved customs broker filing)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (carrier-issued transport document showing dispatch from Canada)
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange settlement evidence (bank or payment-rail receipt from the non-resident buyer)
Commercial invoice and packing list (HS code 9504.40, destination country, declared value, Canadian origin)
Executed zero-rated supply agreement / purchase order from the non-resident customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to documentary audit. Absent an export report, shipping evidence, or foreign-currency settlement proof, CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal four-year period, or indefinitely where misrepresentation, fraud, or willful default exists, and may claw back input tax credits and QST refunds with arrears interest. Gross-negligence penalties of 25% of the assessed amount apply under ETA s.285 and QSTA s.1034. Wilful evasion is prosecutable criminally under ETA s.327 and the Quebec Tax Administration Act, s.169, with fines up to 200% of the amount at issue and imprisonment of up to five years; false customs declarations additionally attract CBSA monetary penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) under the Bank of Canada Act; prudential regulation by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money laundering oversight by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); currency issuance governed by the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a freely floating exchange rate regime with no foreign exchange control legislation; no exchange control permit is required for capital or current account transactions. Capital account is fully convertible, including foreign direct investment, equity injections, dividends, and repatriation of proceeds. Profit remittance by way of dividends to non-resident shareholders is subject to Part XIII federal withholding tax (default 25% under the Income Tax Act, reduced to 5%-15% under applicable tax treaties) and to Quebec dividend withholding tax where applicable under the Taxation Act (CQLR c. I-3); no central bank approval or administrative licence is required for remittance. The only practical hurdles are banking-provided source-of-funds verification and FINTRAC reporting thresholds (e.g., EFT reports for wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory surrender or conversion requirement on export proceeds; exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts, hold foreign currency accounts at Canadian financial institutions, and convert at commercial rates. Filing obligations are limited to FINTRAC reporting (large cross-border currency transfers exceeding CAD 10,000, electronic funds transfer reports) and, for statistical purposes only, Statistics Canada's export/import reporting. No exchange control certificate is needed for commercial trade settlements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payment disbursements; Low for capital escrow and statutory deposit functions. Canadian fintech EMIs operate as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) required to register with FINTRAC and, in Quebec, to hold a money-services business licence from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) under the Money-Services Businesses Act (CQLR c. E-12.000001). Merchants using Stripe or Authorize.Net must treat those processors as MSB/Payment Service Provider counterparts; neither is a bank and neither may hold corporate escrow balances. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Platform Canada, Payoneer, Airwallex) are viable for trade settlement and disbursement sub-accounts, but face de-risking constraints, are not eligible for documentary credit issuance, and cannot act as a substituted reference bank for Quebec commercial registry filings or for investor-side capital escrow undertakings.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted by Canadian Schedule I banks for a Canadian-registered Business Corporation with non-resident directors. Banks accept video-conference KYC interviews where (i) the corporate dossier is notarized and apostilled, (ii) the certificate of incorporation (federal or Quebec) and the Quebec registraire des entreprises attestation are produced, and (iii) the ultimate beneficial owners provide passport copies and proof of address. A Canadian-resident signing officer or a registered agent address is typically required; some banks may condition final approval on an in-person branch visit for shareholders resident in jurisdictions designated as high intensity for money laundering. There is no statutory requirement for physical appearance solely because the entity is a Quebec corporation, but bank-level policy overrides remain at the institution's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with multi-layer holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate tree chart from incorporation registrar; certified certificates of incorporation and good standing for each intermediate entity; apostilled passports of all UBOs; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms (Canada Part XVIII of the Income Tax Act forms); sworn affidavit of control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-match hit against sanctions or politically exposed persons (PEP) lists
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of non-association executed by directors; official passport and proof of birth; negative media screening report from a reputable commercial database; written legal opinion from Canadian counsel confirming no designated person interest; FINTRAC-compliant enhanced due diligence questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source of funds for initial capital injection (collection of trade receivables or shareholder loan)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of shareholder and sponsor bank statements; executed purchase or licensing agreements for trading card intellectual property; invoices for printing and holographic cold-foil equipment; notarized source-of-wealth declaration; audited or reviewed historical financial statements if available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear revenue model of a collectible trading card publisher (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 323111) causing cash-flow mismatch
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Industry profile from NAICS 323111 and ISIC 3240; physical samples of security holographic cold-foil printed cards; executed publisher, distribution, and pre-sale contracts; detailed business plan with projected receivables; list of target retail platforms (Stripe, Authorize.Net reporting snapshots).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office coincident with many other corporate registrations or virtual office flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease agreement for the Quebecregistered office; utility invoice; notarized confirmation from the registered agent; proof of physical presence of the principal officers during the due diligence call; in Quebec, the enterprise registration number (NEQ) attestation evidencing good standing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection must be routed by SWIFT MT103 with the beneficiary Canadian bank account denominated in CAD (or USD if the operating account is a dual-currency account); the payment narrative must state 'share capital contribution' or 'subscription for shares' and reference the share allotment resolution. No exchange control approval is required in Canada; however, the bank may request the executed unanimous shareholders agreement, the directors' resolution authorizing issuance of shares, and the Quebec registraire enterprise update for director and share capital changes. Statistics Canada foreign direct investment reporting is limited to enterprise-level surveys and is not a clearance requirement. FINTRAC EFT reporting applies to transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; the remitting foreign bank must complete an equivalent local report for the outbound leg. Funds should be received only after the account is fully activated and the bank's compliance has cleared the 'source of funds' questionnaire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for supplier payments and trade settlements include: (i) SWIFT MT103 for high-value direct supplier wire transfers (e.g., Korean and US holographic foil printers); (ii) commercial letters of credit issued subject to UCP 600, confirming through correspondent banks for large production runs; (iii) Payments Canada real-time rail (RTR) and the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for domestic same-day CAD payments; (iv) Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for routine CAD cheques and debits; and (v) card network settlements via Stripe and Authorize.Net for e-commerce consumer sales. All international payments exceeding CAD 10,000 must generate FINTRAC EFT reports; documentary compliance requires invoices, customs declarations (B13A export declaration for goods leaving Canada), and if letters of credit are used, full presentation of shipping documents. Funds held in Canada should be swept daily into an interest-bearing operational account, with USD exposure managed via a dual-currency account to reduce conversion friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla CAD/USD FX forwards executed with a Schedule I bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, typical tenors 1-12 months
FX swaps (swap of principal and interest in CAD against USD) for liquidity management
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) referencing CAD, available only through a Canadian-regulated dealer or an international bank with a Canadian securities licence if physical delivery is impractical
Currency options (vanilla calls and puts on CAD/USD) for asymmetric protection on major trade disbursements
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) on any term debt or capital lease obligations to hedge long-term foreign currency repayment exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation or registration in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty CAD 30; continued failure to file for three consecutive years may result in administrative cancellation of the enterprise's legal registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return (if incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty CAD 200; failure to file for two consecutive years may lead to dissolution by the Director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of balance owing plus 1% for each full month late, up to 12 months; repeat-filing penalty 10%; other penalties and interest apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of balance due plus interest; recurring failure may result in additional administrative penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A corporation must appoint an auditor under the QBCA/CBCA unless all shareholders waive the appointment by unanimous resolution for that financial year. No revenue or asset threshold applies to non-reporting private corporations; mandatory audit is imposed for public reporting issuers and for corporations without a valid unanimous waiver.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private corporations, as adopted by the Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the QBCA/CBCA, the corporation must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) and update it within 15 days of any change. The ISC register is not publicly filed; confirmation of shareholding transfers and ISC information is performed annually during the directors' meeting, and any reportable capital changes are disclosed in the Quebec Annual Declaration.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book
